result.markdown: --- title: "Session 4 — Excess Zeros and Model Checking" subtitle: "Expected zeros · structural zeros · zero-inflated and hurdle models · checking fit · autocorrelation · Lab 4" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 3: overdispersion and the negative binomial - Today: **too many zeros**, and **does the model fit?** - By the end you can: - compare **observed and expected zeros** - tell **structural** from **sampling** zeros - fit and judge a **zero-inflated** model - check the fit **over time** and for **leftover correlation** ::: # Topic 1 — Zeros {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Are there too many? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_nb <- MASS::glm.nb(cases ~ fogging + slum + rain_lag1 + month_index + sin(2 * pi * month / 12) + cos(2 * pi * month / 12) + offset(log(population)), data = dg) c(observed = round(mean(dg$cases == 0), 3), nb_expected = round(mean(dnbinom(0, mu = fitted(m_nb), size = m_nb$theta)), 3)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` observed nb_expected 0.202 0.186 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - A good negative binomial **already allows many zeros**: here it expects about **19%** and **20%** are observed, a **small excess** - **More zeros than a count model expects** needs an explanation, not automatically a new model ::: ## Where do the zeros come from? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dg |> group_by(ward) |> summarise(zero_months = sum(cases == 0), mean_cases = round(mean(cases), 1)) |> arrange(desc(zero_months)) |> head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 ward zero_months mean_cases 1 W14 24 0.9 2 W02 21 2.9 3 W04 18 4.1 4 W23 18 11.6 5 W12 16 3.9 6 W20 13 2.8 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} A few wards report **zero for half of the months**. That is not "no dengue": it is **weak surveillance**. These are **structural zeros** (the count process is switched off), as opposed to **sampling zeros** (low mean, no case by chance). ::: # Topic 2 — Zero-inflated models {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Two processes ::: {.eq} P(Y = 0) = pi + (1 - pi) x P~count~(0) P(Y = k) = (1 - pi) x P~count~(k) ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Zero-inflated:** with probability **pi** the ward-month is a structural zero; otherwise counts follow Poisson or NB - **Hurdle:** a binary part (any case?) and a **zero-truncated** count part - Fit with `pscl::zeroinfl(y ~ x | z, dist = "negbin")`: the part after `|` models **pi** ::: ## Fitting it ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_zinb <- zeroinfl(cases ~ fogging + slum + rain_lag1 + month_index + sin(2 * pi * month / 12) + cos(2 * pi * month / 12) + offset(log(population)) | 1, data = dg, dist = "negbin") c(structural_zero_probability = round(plogis(coef(m_zinb, "zero")), 3)); AIC(m_nb, m_zinb) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` structural_zero_probability.(Intercept) 0.06 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` df AIC m_nb 8 5898.446 m_zinb 9 5871.452 ``` ::: ::: ## Be cautious ::: {.warn} - AIC improves, but only modestly here (about 27 points) - **First look for a covariate** that explains the zeros (a reporting-quality indicator): the zero part can then use it (`| reporting`) - Do not add a mixture just because there are zeros: ask **why** - Interpretation: the **count part** gives rate ratios **among at-risk ward-months** ::: # Topic 3 — Checking the fit {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Observed against fitted, over time ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} dg |> mutate(pred = fitted(m_nb)) |> group_by(date) |> summarise(observed = sum(cases), predicted = sum(pred)) |> pivot_longer(c(observed, predicted)) |> ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = name)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Cases", colour = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s4_zeros_checking_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ## Leftover correlation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} w1 <- dg$ward == levels(dg$ward)[1] round(acf(residuals(m_nb, type = "pearson")[w1], plot = FALSE)$acf[1:4], 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1.00 0.13 0.04 -0.06 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Autocorrelation** of residuals within a ward: lag 1 is 0.13, so consecutive months are **somewhat dependent** - Consequence: standard errors **slightly optimistic**; fix with **clustered robust SEs**, random effects, or time-series terms (lagged cases) - Also check **residuals by predictor** and **by ward** ::: ## Model-checking checklist ::: {.good} 1. **Dispersion** and **zeros**: observed vs expected 2. **Observed vs predicted** over time 3. **Autocorrelation** of residuals 4. **Influential** wards: refit leaving one ward out 5. **Sensitivity**: Poisson, NB, zero-inflated: do the **rate ratios** agree? ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 4 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `counts-workshop/labs/lab4_zeros.R` - expected zeros from the NB model; zero months by ward - `pscl::zeroinfl()` and AIC - observed vs predicted over time; `acf()` of residuals ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op8h3n.yhxmmg" data-show="T25seSBhIHNtYWxsIGV4Y2Vzcywgc28gemVyby1pbmZsYXRpb24gaXMgbm90IGNsZWFybHkg bmVlZGVk" data-explain="VGhlIG5lZ2F0aXZlIGJpbm9taWFsIGl0c2VsZiBwcm9kdWNlcyBtYW55IHplcm9zIHdoZW4g dGhlIG1lYW4gaXMgc21hbGwgYW5kIHZhcmlhbmNlIGxhcmdlLiBBIHRpbnkgZXhjZXNzIGRv ZXMgbm90IGJ5IGl0c2VsZiBqdXN0aWZ5IGEgbWl4dHVyZSBtb2RlbC4="} A negative binomial model expects 19% zeros and 20% are observed. What should you conclude? - The model has failed completely and its output is of no use at all - The data cannot be analysed with a count model of any type here - Only a small excess, so zero-inflation is not clearly needed - Every ward has the same chance of recording a zero in a month ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op8ucb.yhy13s" data-show="QSB6ZXJvIGZyb20gYSBwcm9jZXNzIHRoYXQgZ2l2ZXMgbm8gY291bnRzLCBzdWNoIGFzIG5v bi1yZXBvcnRpbmc=" data-explain="U3RydWN0dXJhbCB6ZXJvcyBjb21lIGZyb20gdW5pdHMgdGhhdCBhcmUgbm90IGF0IHJpc2sg b3Igbm90IG9ic2VydmVkIChoZXJlLCB3ZWFrIHN1cnZlaWxsYW5jZSkuIFNhbXBsaW5nIHpl cm9zIGFyaXNlIGJ5IGNoYW5jZSBpbiBhIGNvdW50IHByb2Nlc3Mgd2l0aCBhIHNtYWxsIG1l YW4u"} What is a structural zero? - A zero that arises by chance because the mean count is small here - A zero from a process that gives no counts, such as non-reporting - A zero caused by a coding error in the file that should be fixed first - Any month of the series with fewer than five cases in the ward ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op97l1.yhyfl6" data-show="VGhlIHByb2JhYmlsaXR5IG9mIGEgc3RydWN0dXJhbCB6ZXJvICh0aGUgemVyby1pbmZsYXRp b24gcGFydCk=" data-explain="VGhlIHJpZ2h0LWhhbmQgc2lkZSBhZnRlciB8IHNwZWNpZmllcyB0aGUgbG9naXN0aWMgbW9k ZWwgZm9yIHRoZSB6ZXJvLWluZmxhdGlvbiBwcm9iYWJpbGl0eSBwaS4="} In a zero-inflated model, the part after the vertical bar models what? - The mean of the count process for the ward-months that are at risk - The offset, which is the log of the population of the ward - The probability of a structural zero (the zero-inflation part) - The dispersion parameter theta of the negative binomial count part ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op9ktr.yhyu2k" data-show="RmluZCBvdXQgd2h5LCBhbmQgbG9vayBmb3IgYSBjb3ZhcmlhdGUgdGhhdCBleHBsYWlucyB0 aGVt" data-explain="WmVyb3MgbmVlZCBhbiBleHBsYW5hdGlvbiAocmVwb3J0aW5nLCBhbiBhdC1yaXNrIHBvcHVs YXRpb24pIGJlZm9yZSBjaG9vc2luZyBhIG1vZGVsLiBBIGNvdmFyaWF0ZSBtYXkgcmVtb3Zl IHRoZSBleGNlc3Mgd2l0aG91dCBhIG1peHR1cmUu"} What is the best first step when a model shows more zeros than expected? - Add a zero-inflation term straight away without more thought - Delete every row that contains a zero count from the data - Switch to linear regression on the log of the monthly counts - Find out why, and look for a covariate that explains them ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s4q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="op9y2d.yhz8ju" data-show="TW9udGhzIGFyZSBkZXBlbmRlbnQ7IHN0YW5kYXJkIGVycm9ycyBhcmUgb3B0aW1pc3RpYw==" data-explain="UG9zaXRpdmUgYXV0b2NvcnJlbGF0aW9uIG1lYW5zIG5laWdoYm91cmluZyBtb250aHMgY2Fy cnkgc2hhcmVkIGluZm9ybWF0aW9uLCBzbyB0aGUgZWZmZWN0aXZlIHNhbXBsZSBzaXplIGlz IHNtYWxsZXIgYW5kIFNFcyB0b28gc21hbGwuIFJvYnVzdCBTRXMgb3IgdGltZS1zZXJpZXMg dGVybXMgaGVscC4="} Residuals of a ward over successive months have lag-1 autocorrelation 0.13. What does that imply? - Months are dependent; standard errors are optimistic - The model is perfect and no further checks are needed at all - The ward must be removed from the data before the next fit - The offset has the wrong sign in the model that was fitted ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - Compare **observed and expected zeros** from the fitted model - **Structural** zeros need a reason (reporting); not every excess needs a mixture - `zeroinfl(y ~ x | z, dist = negbin)`; compare **AIC** and **rate ratios** - Check fit **over time**, **autocorrelation** and **influential wards** ::: **Next:** Session 5: reporting and extensions

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
